newsitem.title: JAPAN: Markets positive about NCB restructuring -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Markets positive about NCB restructuring -- MOF.

text.p: The financial markets see Nippon Credit Bank's restructuring plan in a positive light, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Wednesday.
"I think the fact that NCB made up its mind and came up with such a drastic restructuring plan was praised by the market," Mitsuzuka told a news conference.

Nippon Credit Bank, one of three long-term credit banks in Japan, announced on Tuesday that it would cease overseas operations, sell off its Tokyo headquarters as well as other property and write off bad loans totalling 460 billion yen.
On Wednesday shares of NCB fell 38 yen, or 14.56 percent, to 223, making it the top percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Mitsuzuka said the results of the "tankan" survey released by the Bank of Japan (BOJ) earlier in the day largely reflected the economic outlook of the ministry.

"Although there will be negative effects from the consumption tax rise during the April to June quarter, I think the economy, as a whole, will achieve the (government goal of) 1.9 percent growth (for the current fiscal year)," he said.
The BOJ's quarterly survey showed that the business outlook among major manufacturers had improved since the previous survey in November, but had worsened among non-manufacturers.

The key index measuring the mood of major manufacturers improved to plus two in March from minus three in the previous survey last November, the first positive reading since November 1991 and at the higher end of economists' expectations.
But the index for non-manufacturers plunged beyond most expectations to minus six from zero in November.
